ei.title: Seeds as the Best Survival Strategy
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Plants are amazing. Throughout their long existence, they have created diverse survival strategies. Seeds, in particular, are one of the strongest survival techniques they have developed. Let's discover the fascinating and mysterious world of seeds. Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. Jackfruit, the world's largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals' digestive tracts untouched. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds. Many plants opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading them without any return benefit. Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. Devil's claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. Devil's claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. Its blossoms resembling pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals. As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them feel like the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws. That is how devil's claw became known as the worst free rider. Out of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and bury it in the ground to eat or lay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size. Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it were antelope dung. That is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot. They have no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls. By tricking dung beetles into rolling away and burying the seeds, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better. Not all seeds are transported by animals. Some are carried by the wind. This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it spins around. This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and fly farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air using their propellers. The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed to elevate twice as high as non-rotating seeds. As a result, it can travel much farther from the parent tree. The rotation also slows down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground. This helps reduce the damage to the seed during the fall. In most cases, mature seeds are automatically separated from the parent plant. However, some plants only release their seeds after enduring an extreme experience. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. The fallen seeds are conveniently concealed in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided that there is fire.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ tricked → tricking: 전치사 By + 동명사
det.analysis:
✅ ① spotted: 'are often spotted rolling'로 수동태(be p.p.)를 이루어 알맞음

✅ ② confused: 'the confused beetles'로 명사를 수식하는 과거분사로 알맞음

✅ ③ abort: 'but to abort and search'에서 to abort와 (to) search가 병렬을 이루어 알맞음

❌ ④ tricked → tricking: 'By ___ dung beetles'에서 전치사 By 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 tricking이 맞음 ← 정답

questions.passage: The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds ①<u>come</u> out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ starting → started: 수동 의미의 과거분사
det.analysis:
✅ ① come: 복수 주어 the seeds에 맞는 동사원형으로 알맞음

✅ ② concealed: 'are conveniently concealed'로 수동태를 이루어 알맞음

❌ ③ starting → started: 'Wildfire, often ___ by the parent tree'에서 산불이 '시작되는' 수동 의미이므로 과거분사 started가 맞음 ← 정답

✅ ④ provided: 'provided that ~(~라면)'의 접속사로 알맞음

det.korean: ② developing → developed: 현재완료 have + 과거분사
det.analysis:
✅ ① created: 'they have created'로 현재완료(have + p.p.)를 이루어 알맞음

❌ ② developing → developed: 'survival techniques (which) they have developed'에서 현재완료이므로 과거분사 developed가 맞음(have + 현재분사 불가) ← 정답

✅ ③ discover: "Let's discover"에서 Let's 뒤 동사원형으로 알맞음

✅ ④ attracts: 선행사 a sweet smell을 받는 주격 관계대명사 that의 단수 동사로 알맞음

questions.passage: This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with ①<u>smooth</u> ridges on the surface. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① smooth → irregular: 표면에 '불규칙한' 융기
det.analysis:
❌ ① smooth(매끄러운) → irregular(불규칙한): 단풍나무 씨앗은 표면에 '불규칙한' 융기가 있는 부메랑 모양이므로 irregular가 맞음 ← 정답

✅ ② spins: 씨앗이 '빙글빙글 돈다'는 문맥에 적절

✅ ③ longer: 회전으로 공중에 '더 오래' 머문다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ④ elevate: 회전이 씨앗을 두 배 더 높이 '올라가게' 한다는 문맥에 적절

questions.passage: Plants are ①<u>amazing</u>. Throughout their long existence, they have created ②<u>diverse</u> survival strategies. Seeds, in particular, are one of the ③<u>strongest</u> survival techniques they have developed. Let's discover the fascinating and mysterious world of seeds. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ tasteless → tasty: '맛있는' 먹이를 제공
det.analysis:
✅ ① amazing: 식물이 '놀랍다'는 문맥에 적절

✅ ② diverse: 식물이 '다양한' 생존 전략을 만들어 왔다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ③ strongest: 씨앗이 '가장 강력한' 생존 기술 중 하나라는 문맥에 적절

❌ ④ tasteless(맛없는) → tasty(맛있는): 동물을 끌어들이려고 '맛있는' 먹이를 제공하므로 tasty가 맞음 ← 정답

questions.passage: Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it were antelope dung. That is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot. They have no choice but to abort and __________. By tricking dung beetles into rolling away and burying the seeds, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ search for real dung balls(진짜 배설물 덩어리를 찾다)
det.analysis:
씨앗을 먹거나 알을 낳을 수 없다는 것을 깨달은 어리둥절한 쇠똥구리는 포기하고 '진짜 배설물 덩어리를 찾을' 수밖에 없다.

✅ ③ search for real dung balls(진짜 배설물 덩어리를 찾다) ← 정답

❌ ① eat the fake seeds anyway(가짜 씨앗을 그냥 먹다)·② lay their eggs inside them(그 안에 알을 낳다)은 '할 수 없다'는 앞 내용과 반대

❌ ④ roll the seeds back home(씨앗을 집으로 굴려 간다)은 본문 근거 없음
det.tip: have no choice but to + 동사원형: ~할 수밖에 없다

questions.passage: Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are __________. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② securely protected by a strong shell(강한 껍질로 단단히 보호된)
det.analysis:
새들이 eucalyptus 씨앗을 '먹을 수 없는' 이유는 씨앗이 '강한 껍질로 단단히 보호되기' 때문이다.

✅ ② securely protected by a strong shell(강한 껍질로 단단히 보호된) ← 정답

❌ ① easily broken by their sharp beaks(날카로운 부리로 쉽게 부서지는)는 '먹을 수 없다'는 결과와 반대

❌ ③ quickly digested after being eaten(먹힌 뒤 빨리 소화되는)·④ naturally attached to the tree branches(나뭇가지에 자연스럽게 붙은)는 문맥과 무관

ch: easily broken by their sharp beaks
securely protected by a strong shell
naturally attached to the tree branches

questions.stem: 위 글의 silver arrow-reed에 관한 설명으로 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ① 일치하지 않음 — 씨앗은 먹이가 아니라 속임수이다
det.analysis:
❌ ① 쇠똥구리는 씨앗을 먹으려 하지만 먹을 수 없다는 것을 깨닫는다. 씨앗이 '가장 좋아하는 먹이'로 섭취된다는 진술은 본문과 불일치 ← 정답

✅ ② 'spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles'와 일치

✅ ③ 'Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung'과 일치

✅ ④ 'They have no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls'와 일치

ch: 그 씨앗은 쇠똥구리가 가장 좋아하는 먹이여서 영양분으로 섭취된다.
씨앗은 겉모습과 냄새가 영양의 배설물과 매우 유사하다.
쇠똥구리는 결국 포기하고 진짜 배설물 덩어리를 찾을 수밖에 없다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 eucalyptus에 관한 설명으로 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 일치 — 재 속에 감춰져 보호됨
det.analysis:
❌ ① 씨앗은 '모래 알갱이만큼 작고(as tiny as grains of sand)' 강한 껍질로 보호되어 새들이 먹을 수 없으므로 불일치

❌ ② eucalyptus는 '극심한 경험을 견딘 후에야(after enduring an extreme experience)' 씨앗을 방출하므로 '언제나 자동으로'는 불일치

❌ ③ 산불은 경쟁 식물들을 '파괴하므로(destroying other plants)' 보호한다는 진술은 불일치

✅ ④ 'conveniently concealed in the soft ash ~ which protects them from the harsh environment'와 일치 ← 정답
det.tip: 씨앗=작음/불에 방출/재 속 보호, 산불=경쟁 식물 파괴

ch: 씨앗이 크고 무거워 새들이 쉽게 먹을 수 있다.
산불은 씨앗 주변의 다른 식물들을 보호해 준다.
떨어진 씨앗은 부드러운 재 속에 감춰져 가혹한 환경으로부터 보호된다.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 일치 — 회전이 낙하 속도를 늦춰 손상을 줄임
det.analysis:
❌ ① '일부(Some)'가 바람에 의해 운반되는 것이지 '모든' 씨앗은 아니므로 불일치

questions.passage: As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals. As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them feel like <u>the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws</u>. That is how devil's claw became known as the worst free rider.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 갈고리가 동물에게 극심한 통증을 일으킨다

밑줄 친 표현은 붙어 있는 갈고리가 유발하는 '심한 통증(severe pain)'을, 마치 악마가 섬뜩한 발톱으로 할퀴는 것처럼 비유한 것이다.

✅ ③ 갈고리가 동물에게 극심한 통증을 일으킨다 ← 정답

❌ ② 갈고리가 스스로 사냥한다는 내용은 없음

❌ ④ 악마가 보호해 준다는 의미가 아님
det.tip: 비유 표현 = 갈고리로 인한 극심한 통증

questions.passage: Jackfruit, the world's largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals' digestive tracts untouched. When <u>these animals</u> poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 these animals가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① 맛있는 과육을 먹은 동물들
det.analysis:
밑줄 친 these animals는 앞 문장의 '과육을 먹고 그것을 소화하는 동물들(the animals that consume it)'을 가리킨다.

✅ ① 맛있는 과육을 먹은 동물들 ← 정답

❌ ②③④는 본문에서 과육을 먹는 동물과 무관한 대상
det.tip: these animals = 과육(fruit flesh)을 먹는 동물들

questions.passage: This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and fly farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air using their propellers. The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed to elevate __________. As a result, it can travel much farther from the parent tree. The rotation also slows down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground.

det.korean: ② twice as high as non-rotating seeds(회전하지 않는 씨앗보다 두 배 더 높이)
det.analysis:
날개에 의한 회전은 단풍나무 씨앗을 '회전하지 않는 씨앗보다 두 배 더 높이' 올라가게 하여, 결과적으로 모체 나무로부터 훨씬 더 멀리 이동하게 한다.

✅ ② twice as high as non-rotating seeds(회전하지 않는 씨앗보다 두 배 더 높이) ← 정답

❌ ① slightly lower ~(약간 더 낮게)는 'elevate(올라가다)'와 반대

❌ ③ half as far ~·④ three times deeper ~는 본문 수치와 맞지 않음
det.tip: 배수 표현: 배수사 + as + 원급 + as (두 배 더 ~한)
